subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron get a dedicated `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or wait for the broader per-session policy design?
rationale: This changes a public config/security boundary and must define precedence with existing cron `toolsAllow`, inherited caps, delivery fallback, and CLI backend behavior before implementation.

options.title: Add Dedicated Cron Policy
options.body: Add `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence and tests so operators can set cron defaults without overloading subagent semantics.

options.title: Inherit Subagent Policy
options.body: Treat cron sessions as subagent-like for tool policy, reducing new config surface but coupling two distinct execution scopes.

options.title: Wait For Broader Policy RFC
options.body: Defer this issue into the broader per-session policy design, leaving only per-job `--tools` and current delivery safeguards for now.

recommendation.title: Add Dedicated Cron Policy
recommendation.body: Add `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence and tests so operators can set cron defaults without overloading subagent semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent commit trail through cron message-tool behavior and the CLI toolsAllow follow-up that any policy decision must preserve.
